config_name: Legion Go 2 — AMD Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme (8C/16T) / Radeon 890M 16CU, 16GB LPDDR5X-8000, 512GB NVMe, 8.8" 2560x1600 144Hz OLED

specs.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme (Zen 5, 8-core/16-thread, up to ~5.0GHz)
specs.ports: 2x USB4 40Gbps (DP alt-mode, PD 3.0), 3.5mm, microSD UHS-II; no HDMI
specs.keyboard_notes: no keyboard; detachable Legion TrueStrike controllers (hall-effect sticks, 3ms low-latency mode, rear mappable buttons, touchpad in right controller)

battery.notes: Identical 74.25Wh battery and APU as the 32GB/1TB tier — no battery delta. Estimate ~6-8h light use, ~3.5-5h gaming at 2560x1600; not pro-verified this session.

price.store: lenovo.com/ca (Best Buy CA also stocks the line)
price.notes: C$1,549 carried over from research/parts/handhelds/LIST.md (est). Not verifiable this session (BBY API DNS failure, lenovo.com bot-walled). Only ~C$250 below the 32GB/1TB tier — the 32GB config is usually the better buy; choose this one only when discounted.

reviews.quote: Gaming handheld with great 144 Hz OLED and detachable controllers; however, the price comes in at a hefty €1,499, making it one of the most expensive handhelds on the market.

reviews.outlet: Engadget (2026 Steam Deck re-check, mentions Legion Go 2)
reviews.quote: competitors (Xbox Ally/Ally X, Legion Go 2) beat it in raw Time Spy, but in real-world applications, Valve's handheld often comes out on top

praises: Same Z2 Extreme + Radeon 890M and same 8.8" 144Hz OLED as the flagship tier — zero performance or display compromise vs the C$1,799 model
Detachable TrueStrike controllers with hall-effect sticks and the 3ms low-latency mode are identical across tiers
C$1,549 makes it the cheapest way into the Go 2's screen and detachable-controller design in Canada
512GB M.2 2242 SSD is user-replaceable and the UHS-II microSD slot covers library growth cheaply
Full Windows 11 runs Game Pass and anti-cheat titles that SteamOS handhelds cannot, even at 16GB
complaints: 16GB is the tight spot: newer AAA at 2560x1600 plus Windows background load can push into paging, and the RAM is soldered with no upgrade path
512GB fills almost immediately — a few current AAA games at this resolution eat the whole drive
Only ~C$250 separates it from the 32GB/1TB tier, so the value case is weak unless this SKU is on sale
~982g with controllers is still the heaviest mainstream handheld, and the glossy 500-nit OLED is poor outdoors
Same no-webcam and Windows wake/sleep frustrations as the flagship tier

standouts: Cheapest Canadian entry into the Go 2's 8.8" 144Hz OLED and detachable-controller design
Identical CPU/GPU/display to the flagship tier — the performance story is unchanged
dealbreakers: 16GB soldered RAM at 2560x1600 is the practical floor for newer AAA, with no upgrade path
Nearly 1kg in-hand and no webcam — same portability/ergonomics liabilities as the flagship
design_philosophy: Lenovo builds the Legion Go 2 as a detachable-controller Windows tablet first and a handheld console second, and every tier shares the same screen, APU and controllers — the tiers buy you memory headroom, not capability. This 16GB/512GB entry is the access point of that philosophy: the full design idea at the lowest Canadian price, but with the soldered-RAM ceiling that makes the desktop-mode pitch weaker than on the 32GB flagship.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from the 32GB/1TB anchor entry (05.json), which is itself delta-derived from the verified Steam Deck OLED anchor (see SHARED-legion-go2.md) — professional scores unverified. Sibling deltas from the anchor: productivity -0.5 and creative_work -0.5 (16GB vs 32GB for multitask/heavier work), gaming -0.3 (16GB at 2560x1600 is the practical floor for newer AAA; paging pressure). Everything else identical: same APU, GPU, battery, display, chassis and controllers. Handheld conventions from SHARED-steam-deck.md: screen_size kept modest (5.5) with portability carrying the form-factor story; keyboard_trackpad 1.0 (no keyboard; touchpad is inside the right controller); pen_touch 4.0 (multi-touch yes, no pen). Omitted tier: a 32GB/2TB variant exists in some markets but Canadian retail availability/pricing could not be confirmed this session. Image URL is a real Commons photo of the first-gen Legion Go (wrong generation, best verified direct image available). Z2 Extreme iGPU is the Radeon 890M (16 CU RDNA 3.5).
